questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To learn more about the culture and get to experience new connections.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing. I got to know so many people and had a wonderful half year.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that hard. Most things just took a lot of time to receive.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from my buddy through the ELSA buddy program. I was also able to ask the administration for documents and so on if I needed them. The day to day things I had to find a solution on myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I rented an air BnB apartment with another KU student.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Only rent an apartment through a safe website or people you know. There are a lot of scammers so be aware.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university was helping a lot of other students if they hadn't found a place when school started.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university was really helpful so the overall time I put into it was not that long. It just took a lot of time to receive the approvals on the different documents.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to write a motivational letter and send additional material. I had to choose some courses. When I wrote the host university to get more insight on what the courses contained it was pretty easy from there. As stated before it just took a lot of time to get the approval after I sent the documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write the contact provided by the host university. She was not always available in the application period but in the end, I figured it out on my own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for all the information you can get about the courses from the beginning. Start the process early on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All exams had to be handwritten.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had master-level, LL-M and license courses, which I needed to do to get 30 points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any courses where books were needed so I just had to write down what the teachers said and learn it by heart.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Law (GB) – 6 ECTS
Intellectual property – 8 ECTS
English equity and trust law – 6 ECTS
Company law – 8 ECTS
Torts – 3 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: English equity and trust law was the most interesting course that I had because the teacher was amazing and he really interacted. The torts course was the class I got the most out of.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I didn't realize it would be so expensive to travel if it was not in the heart of Paris. I recommend buying a metrocard ("NAVIGO"). Eating out was way cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs and such.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything from football to poetry clubs. There were many things you could join in on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the ELSA program - They have a tour day where they show you around Paris. There are also Erasmus Facebook groups that offer trips in France where you can get to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All museums are free for students under 25 so go to different museums. Go on trips in France - the rapid train is super fast so you can get around easily.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It's very similar to Denmark. Just remember to watch out for your things because there is a lot of thieves.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join in on the intro days and be open-minded. And join in on the different activities that are offered.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language could be a barrier sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the wine and the social vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look out for your phone because it is your most important tool and phone thieves are pretty common in Paris. Bring a folder with all the important information you will need including a printed version of insurance papers, so you know who to call if/when something gets stolen. Remember to study a little along the way so you are able to enjoy the last month as well although it is the examperiode.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to socialize. It's the people around you that makes the trip worth it. And bring pens and paper for the exams and note-taking.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The relationships, the food experience and so on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The waiting time. You need to bring your patience as well.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
